goal: Get comfortable seeing Hangul as sound blocks, not English letters in disguise.
scenario: A first quiet study session where the learner reads one block, hears it, and repeats it back.

dialogue.speaker: Tutor
dialogue.en: Today we'll look at just one character. It's 한.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.ko: 한... 천천히 한 번만 더 말해 주세요.
dialogue.romanization: han... cheoncheonhi han beonman deo malhae juseyo.
dialogue.en: Han... please say it slowly one more time.

dialogue.speaker: Tutor
dialogue.ko: 좋아요. 한은 ㅎ, ㅏ, ㄴ이 같이 있어요.
dialogue.romanization: joayo. haneun hieut, a, nieuni gachi isseoyo.
dialogue.en: Good. 한 has ㅎ, ㅏ, and ㄴ together.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Ah, now I'll look at the Hangul first.

realLifeTask: Ask someone to say one Korean word slowly, then read the Hangul before checking romanization.
checkpoints: I can see 한 as ㅎ + ㅏ + ㄴ.
I can ask 천천히 한 번만 더 말해 주세요.
I check Hangul first and use romanization only as backup.

sampleAnswer.ko: 천천히 한 번만 더 말해 주세요.
sampleAnswer.romanization: cheoncheonhi han beonman deo malhae juseyo.
sampleAnswer.en: Please say it slowly one more time.

goal: Start a first meeting politely and say your name without freezing.
scenario: A language exchange table where two people meet for the first time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Hello. Nice to meet you for the first time.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Hello. I'm Hana.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I'm Minjun. Nice to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Nice to meet you too. I look forward to studying together.

realLifeTask: Say hello, give your name, and close with one polite friendly line.
checkpoints: I can say 안녕하세요 without looking at English.
I can say 저는 ___예요 with my own name.
I can close a first meeting with 만나서 반가워요 or 잘 부탁드려요.

sampleAnswer.ko: 안녕하세요. 저는 하나예요. 만나서 반가워요.
sampleAnswer.en: Hello. I'm Hana. Nice to meet you.

goal: Point at people and things around you and say what they are.
scenario: A cafe table with a menu, a notebook, and two people introducing themselves.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What is this?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: This is a menu. That is my notebook.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I'm a student. What about you, Hana?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I'm an office worker.

realLifeTask: Use 이건/저는 and say two noun sentences about your table or yourself.
checkpoints: I can ask 이건 뭐예요?
I can choose 이에요 or 예요 from the noun ending.
I can use 저는 to set myself as the topic.

sampleAnswer.ko: 이건 메뉴예요. 저는 학생이에요.
sampleAnswer.en: This is a menu. I'm a student.

goal: Ask what exists, say what you have, and say what is missing.
scenario: A small restaurant visit where the learner asks about seats and reservations.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Do you have a reservation?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: No, I don't have a reservation. Is there a seat?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Yes, there is a seat by the window.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Great. I have time too.

realLifeTask: Ask whether there is a seat, bathroom, or reservation, then answer with 있어요 or 없어요.
checkpoints: I can ask 자리 있어요? or 화장실 있어요?
I can say 예약이 없어요 without using 을/를.
I can use 이/가 for the thing that exists or is missing.

sampleAnswer.ko: 예약이 없어요. 자리 있어요?
sampleAnswer.en: I don't have a reservation. Is there a seat?

goal: Talk about simple daily actions and the thing you do them to.
scenario: A morning check-in about breakfast, coffee, studying, and reading.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Are you eating breakfast today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes, I eat breakfast and drink coffee.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Are you studying Korean again today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes. At night I read a little.

realLifeTask: Say two things you do today and one object you use with 을/를.
checkpoints: I can say 먹어요, 마셔요, 공부해요, and 읽어요.
I can add 을/를 when the action has an object.
I can connect two daily actions with 고.

sampleAnswer.ko: 아침을 먹고 커피를 마셔요.
sampleAnswer.en: I eat breakfast and drink coffee.

goal: Say where you go and where something happens without mixing up 에 and 에서.
scenario: A simple plan to go to a cafe and meet a friend there.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Where are you going today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I'm going to a cafe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What are you doing at the cafe?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I'm meeting a friend at the cafe.

realLifeTask: Say one place you go to and one thing you do there.
checkpoints: I can use 에 for the destination: 카페에 가요.
I can use 에서 for the action place: 카페에서 만나요.
I can avoid 카페에서 가요 when I mean going to the cafe.

sampleAnswer.ko: 카페에 가요. 카페에서 친구를 만나요.
sampleAnswer.en: I'm going to a cafe. I'm meeting a friend at the cafe.

goal: Order something small and pay without overthinking the sentence.
scenario: A cafe counter where the learner orders a drink and asks about card payment.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Would you like to order?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: One Americano, please.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Would you like it hot?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Yes. And is card payment okay?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Yes, card is okay.

realLifeTask: Order one drink or food item and ask if card payment is okay.
checkpoints: I can order with N 주세요.
I can use one counter like 한 잔 or 하나.
I can ask 카드 돼요? in a simple shop situation.

sampleAnswer.ko: 아메리카노 한 잔 주세요. 카드 돼요?
sampleAnswer.romanization: amerikano han jan juseyo. kadeu dwaeyo?
sampleAnswer.en: One Americano, please. Is card payment okay?

goal: Say what you want, what you can do, and what you cannot do today.
scenario: Two friends trying to choose food and make a small plan.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What do you want to eat today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I want to eat bibimbap.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Then can you go now?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 지금은 못 가요. 한 시간 후에 갈 수 있어요.
dialogue.romanization: jigeumeun mot gayo. han sigan hue gal su isseoyo.
dialogue.en: I can't go now. I can go in an hour.

realLifeTask: Say one thing you want to do, one thing you can do, and one thing you cannot do today.
checkpoints: I can say V고 싶어요 for something I want.
I can say Vㄹ/을 수 있어요 for something possible.
I can use 못 for a real limitation, not just preference.

sampleAnswer.ko: 비빔밥을 먹고 싶어요. 지금은 못 가요.
sampleAnswer.romanization: bibimbabeul meokgo sipeoyo. jigeumeun mot gayo.
sampleAnswer.en: I want to eat bibimbap. I can't go now.

goal: Ask for help, ask permission, and understand a polite no.
scenario: A museum or store where the learner wants help and asks whether photos are okay.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Excuse me, please help me a little.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Sure, what can I help you with?

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Is it okay to take photos here?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Sorry, but please don't take photos here.

realLifeTask: Ask for help, ask if one action is okay, and respond politely if the answer is no.
checkpoints: I can soften a request with 죄송한데.
I can ask permission with 아/어도 돼요?
I can recognize 지 마세요 as a polite prohibition.

sampleAnswer.ko: 죄송한데, 여기에서 사진 찍어도 돼요?
sampleAnswer.en: Excuse me, is it okay to take photos here?

goal: Ask for directions or repetition when you are lost or missed something.
scenario: A station or hotel lobby where the learner needs one clear answer.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: Excuse me, where is the bathroom?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: It's over there on the right.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.ko: 다시 한 번만 천천히 말해 주세요.
dialogue.romanization: dasi han beonman cheoncheonhi malhae juseyo.
dialogue.en: Please say it slowly one more time.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Sure. It's over there on the right.

dialogue.speaker: Learner
dialogue.en: I understand. Thank you.

realLifeTask: Ask where something is, then ask the person to repeat slowly.
checkpoints: I can begin politely with 죄송한데.
I can ask 어디예요? for a place I need.
I can ask 다시 한 번만 천천히 말해 주세요.

sampleAnswer.ko: 화장실이 어디예요? 다시 한 번만 천천히 말해 주세요.
sampleAnswer.romanization: hwajangsiri eodiyeyo? dasi han beonman cheoncheonhi malhae juseyo.
sampleAnswer.en: Where is the bathroom? Please say it slowly one more time.

goal: Connect two small ideas so your Korean sounds like a real short explanation.
scenario: Two friends changing plans because one person is busy.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Why can't you come today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I can't go because I have work.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Then if you have time, shall we meet tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Sounds good. I'll call after I finish.

realLifeTask: Explain why you cannot do something today, then make one simple next plan.
checkpoints: I can connect a reason with 아서/어서.
I can make a simple condition with 면.
I can promise the next action with ㄹ/을게요.

sampleAnswer.ko: 일이 있어서 못 가요. 끝나고 전화할게요.
sampleAnswer.romanization: iri isseoseo mot gayo. kkeunnago jeonhwahalgeyo.
sampleAnswer.en: I can't go because I have work. I'll call after I finish.

goal: Say what you think without sounding too blunt.
scenario: A friend asks what you thought of a movie, cafe, class, or app.
realLifeTask: Give one opinion, add a reason, and soften it with 제 생각에는, 좀, or 것 같아요.
checkpoints: I can start softly with 제 생각에는 or 저는.
I can give a reason with -거든요 or -아서/어서.
I can use 것 같아요 when I want the opinion to feel less direct.

sampleAnswer.ko: 제 생각에는 조금 비싸지만 괜찮은 것 같아요.
sampleAnswer.en: I think it is a little expensive, but it seems okay.

goal: Talk about a cultural or social topic and report what someone said.
scenario: You read a short post about Korean culture and tell a friend the main point.
realLifeTask: Report one thing you heard, read, or learned using -다고 해요 or -라고 해요.
checkpoints: I can report a noun sentence with -이라고/라고 해요.
I can report an adjective or verb sentence with -다고 해요.
I can keep my own opinion separate from what someone else said.

sampleAnswer.ko: 한국에서는 약속 시간을 지키는 게 중요하다고 해요.
sampleAnswer.en: They say keeping appointment times is important in Korea.

goal: Talk through a work or money decision in a realistic, cautious way.
scenario: A friend is deciding whether to start a job, buy something, or try a side project.
realLifeTask: Say one decision you made and one worry you still have.
checkpoints: I can use -기로 했어요 for a decision.
I can use -ㄹ까 봐 걱정돼요 for a worry.
I can add 그래도 when I will try anyway.

sampleAnswer.ko: 이번 달에는 돈을 조금 아끼기로 했어요. 그래도 한국어 수업은 계속하려고요.
sampleAnswer.en: I decided to save a little money this month. Still, I plan to continue Korean class.

goal: Describe feelings with a little more honesty and nuance.
scenario: After a presentation, test, date, or awkward message, you tell a friend how it felt.
realLifeTask: Describe one feeling, then add what you pretended or almost did.
checkpoints: I can use -는 척했어요 when I acted differently from how I felt.
I can use -ㄹ 뻔했어요 for something that almost happened.
I can soften emotional sentences with 좀 or 사실.

sampleAnswer.ko: 사실 좀 떨렸는데 괜찮은 척했어요.
sampleAnswer.en: Honestly, I was a little nervous, but I pretended I was okay.

goal: Make one longer sentence that still feels easy to follow.
scenario: You explain why you practiced, what your purpose was, and what changed after that.
realLifeTask: Connect cause, purpose, and result in two short Korean sentences.
checkpoints: I can use -길래 for a reason I reacted to.
I can use -기 위해서 for purpose.
I can use -ㄹ수록 when something changes more and more.

sampleAnswer.ko: 발표가 있어서 집에서 연습했어요. 연습할수록 조금 더 자연스러워져요.
sampleAnswer.en: I practiced at home because I had a presentation. The more I practice, the more natural it gets.

goal: Answer what you did yesterday with one clean past-tense sentence.
scenario: A friend asks about yesterday's evening, weekend, or class.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What did you do yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yesterday I watched a movie with a friend.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: How was it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: It was fun. But the weather was a bit cold.

realLifeTask: Answer 어제 뭐 했어요? with one real past-tense action and one short feeling.
checkpoints: I can make 봤어요, 먹었어요, 갔어요, 왔어요, and 했어요.
I can add one feeling such as 좋았어요 or 재미있었어요.
I can catch common irregular mistakes like 춥었어요.

sampleAnswer.ko: 어제 친구랑 저녁을 먹었어요. 정말 좋았어요.
sampleAnswer.en: Yesterday I ate dinner with a friend. It was really nice.

naturalWhy.title: Why past tense sounds natural here
naturalWhy.todayScene: Someone asks 어제 뭐 했어요? The time word 어제 already tells the listener the event is finished.
naturalWhy.why: 어제 points to a finished time, so Korean expects the verb ending to match that finished feeling. 봐요 sounds like now, usually, or a future plan. 봤어요 closes the event and matches 어제.
koreanSense: 오늘 봐요 feels present or scheduled.
어제 봤어요 feels finished and easy to understand.
내일 볼 거예요 points forward, so it should not use past tense.

goal: Say a real future plan, not just a grammar example.
scenario: You are making a weekend or evening plan with someone.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What are you going to do this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: I am going to meet a friend and go to a cafe.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: What if it rains?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: If it rains, I am going to study at home.

realLifeTask: Answer 주말에 뭐 할 거예요? and add what you will do if the plan changes.
checkpoints: I can use -(으)ㄹ 거예요 for a plan or prediction.
I can use -면 for a simple condition.
I can tell apart 할 거예요 from 할게요.

sampleAnswer.ko: 주말에는 카페에서 공부할 거예요. 비가 오면 집에서 할 거예요.
sampleAnswer.en: This weekend I am going to study at a cafe. If it rains, I will do it at home.

goal: Ask better follow-up questions so the conversation does not stop.
scenario: You are getting to know a classmate, tutor, or language partner.
realLifeTask: Ask three follow-up questions using 어디, 언제, 왜, 어떻게, or 누구.
checkpoints: I can pick the question word that matches the missing answer.
I can keep the question word in the Korean answer slot.
I can ask a short follow-up like 왜요? or 언제부터요?

sampleAnswer.ko: 언제부터 한국어를 공부했어요? 보통 어떻게 연습해요?
sampleAnswer.en: Since when have you studied Korean? How do you usually practice?

goal: Use numbers for real times, prices, ages, and counts.
scenario: You set a meeting time and check a price before buying something.
realLifeTask: Say one time, one price, and one count from your actual day.
checkpoints: I can use native Korean numbers for hours and counters.
I can use Sino-Korean numbers for minutes, dates, and prices.
I can avoid mixing 세 시 and 삼 분 the wrong way.

sampleAnswer.ko: 세 시 십 분에 만나요. 커피 두 잔은 오천 원이에요.
sampleAnswer.en: Let's meet at 3:10. Two cups of coffee are 5,000 won.

goal: Describe the exact person or thing you mean.
scenario: You are pointing out the right bag, person, app, or place.
realLifeTask: Make two noun phrases before a noun, like 자주 쓰는 앱 or 작은 가방.
checkpoints: I can put adjective descriptions before nouns.
I can use V-는 N for present or habitual action descriptions.
I can turn a full sentence into a useful noun phrase.

sampleAnswer.ko: 제가 자주 쓰는 앱이에요. 화면이 깔끔한 앱이라서 좋아요.
sampleAnswer.en: It is an app I use often. I like it because the screen is clean.

goal: Compare two choices and say what fits your taste.
scenario: You are choosing food, drinks, movies, hobbies, or study methods.
realLifeTask: Compare two real options and say which one you like more.
checkpoints: I can use 보다 더 for a simple comparison.
I can use 만큼 when two things are similar in degree.
I can use 제 취향에 맞아요 for taste and preference.

sampleAnswer.ko: 저는 차보다 커피를 더 좋아해요. 이 카페가 제 취향에 맞아요.
sampleAnswer.en: I like coffee more than tea. This cafe fits my taste.

goal: Explain where to go and how to get there.
scenario: You ask for a subway exit, direction, or transport choice.
realLifeTask: Give one short route using 로/으로 for direction or transport.
checkpoints: I can use 로/으로 for direction, route, and transport method.
I can use -(으)러 가요 for going to do something.
I can ask 몇 번 출구로 가요? when I need an exit.

sampleAnswer.ko: 지하철로 가세요. 삼 번 출구로 나가서 오른쪽으로 가세요.
sampleAnswer.en: Go by subway. Go out exit three and go to the right.

goal: Suggest trying something without sounding pushy.
scenario: You suggest food, clothing, an app, or a study method to a friend.
realLifeTask: Make one gentle suggestion with 한번 -아/어 보세요 or -아/어 볼까요?
checkpoints: I can use -아/어 보다 for trying an action.
I can use -아/어 보세요 as a gentle suggestion.
I can use -ㄹ까요? when deciding together.

sampleAnswer.ko: 이 앱 한번 써 보세요. 단어 복습하기 좋아요.
sampleAnswer.en: Try this app once. It is good for reviewing vocabulary.

goal: Say 'but' and 'even though' with the right amount of contrast.
scenario: A plan is good but expensive, rainy but still worth doing, or hard but useful.
realLifeTask: Describe one mixed situation using -지만, 그런데, or -아/어도.
checkpoints: I can use -지만 inside one sentence.
I can use 그런데 when the next sentence changes direction.
I can use -아/어도 when the problem does not stop the result.

sampleAnswer.ko: 이 식당은 조금 비싸지만 맛있어요. 사람이 많아도 기다릴 만해요.
sampleAnswer.en: This restaurant is a little expensive, but it is tasty. Even if there are many people, it is worth waiting.

goal: Make a careful guess from what you can see or hear.
scenario: You infer why someone is late, tired, busy, or quiet.
realLifeTask: Look at one situation and make a soft guess using -나 봐요 or 것 같아요.
checkpoints: I can use -나 봐요 when I infer from a clue.
I can use 것 같아요 for a softer guess or opinion.
I can avoid using a guess form when I already know the fact.

sampleAnswer.ko: 비가 많이 와서 길이 막히나 봐요. 조금 늦을 것 같아요.
sampleAnswer.en: It looks like traffic is bad because it is raining a lot. I think I will be a little late.

goal: Say what is happening right now or what you are in the middle of doing.
scenario: Someone texts while you are studying, cooking, commuting, or waiting.
realLifeTask: Reply to 지금 뭐 해요? with one ongoing action.
checkpoints: I can use -고 있어요 for an action in progress.
I can add 지금, 아직, or 계속 to clarify timing.
I can choose 있다/없다 carefully when the verb already includes a state.

sampleAnswer.ko: 지금 카페에서 한국어를 공부하고 있어요.
sampleAnswer.en: I am studying Korean at a cafe right now.

goal: Tell a simple sequence without making the listener guess the order.
scenario: You explain what you did before class, after work, or right after arriving.
realLifeTask: Tell three small steps using -고 나서, -자마자, or -기 전에.
checkpoints: I can use -고 나서 after one action is complete.
I can use -자마자 for immediately after.
I can use -기 전에 for before doing something.

sampleAnswer.ko: 수업 전에 커피를 샀어요. 집에 오자마자 복습했어요.
sampleAnswer.en: Before class I bought coffee. As soon as I came home, I reviewed.

goal: Explain when an action changed, got interrupted, or ended in a new state.
scenario: You started one plan, but something happened while you were doing it.
realLifeTask: Describe one interrupted or changed plan using -다가 or -아/어 있다.
checkpoints: I can use -다가 when one action is interrupted or changes.
I can use -아/어 있다 for a state that remains after an action.
I can keep the before-and-after order clear.

sampleAnswer.ko: 공부하다가 친구 전화를 받았어요. 노트북은 아직 켜져 있어요.
sampleAnswer.en: I was studying and then got a call from a friend. The laptop is still on.

goal: Explain a cause and an unexpected result naturally.
scenario: Weather, traffic, mistakes, or sudden plans changed what happened.
realLifeTask: Say one thing that happened because of a problem using -아서/어서 or -는 바람에.
checkpoints: I can use -아서/어서 for ordinary cause and result.
I can use -는 바람에 for an unwanted or unexpected result.
I can avoid using -아서/어서 with commands or suggestions.

sampleAnswer.ko: 비가 많이 오는 바람에 약속에 늦었어요.
sampleAnswer.en: Because it rained a lot, I was late for the appointment.

goal: Talk about purpose and time span in one clear plan.
scenario: You study for a test, save money for a trip, or work from one time to another.
realLifeTask: Say what you are doing for a purpose and from when to when.
checkpoints: I can use -기 위해서 for purpose.
I can use 전에 and 후에 around events.
I can use 부터 and 까지 for a time or place range.

sampleAnswer.ko: 시험을 위해서 월요일부터 금요일까지 공부할 거예요.
sampleAnswer.en: For the test, I will study from Monday to Friday.

goal: Describe decisions and changes that happened over time.
scenario: You decided to start a habit, changed a plan, or something became easier.
realLifeTask: Say one decision and one change using -기로 했어요 and -게 됐어요.
checkpoints: I can use -기로 했어요 for a decision.
I can use -게 됐어요 for a change that came to happen.
I can use -아/어지다 for becoming a new state.

sampleAnswer.ko: 매일 십 분씩 듣기로 했어요. 그래서 조금 익숙해졌어요.
sampleAnswer.en: I decided to listen for ten minutes every day. So I became a little more used to it.

goal: Choose a speech level that fits the person in front of you.
scenario: You switch between a friend, a teacher, a customer, and a text chat.
realLifeTask: Rewrite one idea in polite, formal, and casual styles.
checkpoints: I can use 해요체 as the safe everyday default.
I can recognize formal -습니다 style.
I can avoid using 반말 unless the relationship clearly allows it.

sampleAnswer.ko: 지금 가요. 지금 갑니다. 지금 가.
sampleAnswer.en: I'm going now. I am going now. I'm going.

goal: Show respect without making every sentence overly formal.
scenario: You talk about a teacher, boss, parent, or older customer.
realLifeTask: Make one sentence about a respected person using -(으)시- and one honorific word.
checkpoints: I can add -(으)시- when the subject deserves respect.
I can use words like 드시다, 계시다, 말씀하시다, and 댁.
I can separate subject honorifics from listener politeness.

sampleAnswer.ko: 선생님께서 지금 사무실에 계세요.
sampleAnswer.en: The teacher is in the office now.

goal: Bring up background information without sounding abrupt.
scenario: A file is late, a plan changed, or you need to disagree gently.
realLifeTask: Write a short message using 사실은 plus -는데요, -거든요, or -잖아요.
checkpoints: I can use -는데요 to open background softly.
I can use -거든요 for new background the listener may not know.
I can use -잖아요 only when the listener likely knows or agrees.

sampleAnswer.ko: 사실은 자료가 아직 안 끝났는데요. 어제 갑자기 일이 생겼거든요.
sampleAnswer.en: Actually, the materials are not finished yet. Something suddenly came up yesterday.

goal: Report what you personally saw or noticed changing.
scenario: You watched something happen and now explain what changed after that.
realLifeTask: Describe one thing you directly saw, heard, or noticed using -더라고요 or -더니.
checkpoints: I can use -더라고요 for something I personally observed.
I can use -더니 when one observed situation led to a change.
I can avoid using plain -더니 for my own neutral actions.

sampleAnswer.ko: 아까는 사람이 별로 없더라고요. 그런데 조금 지나더니 줄이 길어졌어요.
sampleAnswer.en: Earlier there were not many people. But after a bit, the line got long.

goal: Pass along what someone said without making it sound like your own words.
scenario: You tell a coworker, classmate, or friend what another person said or asked.
realLifeTask: Report one statement and one question from someone else.
checkpoints: I can use -다고 했어요 for reported statements.
I can use -냐고 했어요 for reported questions.
I can keep tense and speaker perspective clear.

sampleAnswer.ko: 민수 씨가 오늘 늦는다고 했어요. 몇 시에 시작하냐고도 물어봤어요.
sampleAnswer.en: Minsu said he will be late today. He also asked what time it starts.

goal: Build longer noun phrases and describe passive situations clearly.
scenario: A door is closed, a file was uploaded, or a thing you found needs description.
realLifeTask: Describe one object with a modifier and one passive result.
checkpoints: I can make a noun phrase before the noun.
I can use passive forms when the subject receives the action.
I can avoid mixing passive and causative meanings.

sampleAnswer.ko: 어제 받은 파일이 열리지 않아요.
sampleAnswer.en: The file I received yesterday will not open.

goal: Say something almost happened, or that there is no choice but to do it.
scenario: You nearly missed a train, almost made a mistake, or have only one option.
realLifeTask: Describe one almost-happened situation and one unavoidable action.
checkpoints: I can use -ㄹ 뻔했어요 for almost happened.
I can use -ㄹ 수밖에 없어요 for no real choice.
I can use 만 to narrow the option or limit.

sampleAnswer.ko: 지하철을 놓칠 뻔했어요. 그래서 택시를 탈 수밖에 없었어요.
sampleAnswer.en: I almost missed the subway. So I had no choice but to take a taxi.

goal: Hedge a guess or regret so it sounds socially natural.
scenario: You are not fully sure, or you wish you had done something differently.
realLifeTask: Make one soft guess and one small regret.
checkpoints: I can use 것 같아요 and -나 봐요 with different levels of evidence.
I can use -ㄹ걸요 for a careful prediction.
I can use -ㄹ걸 그랬어요 for regret.

sampleAnswer.ko: 오늘 사람이 많을 것 같아요. 예약할걸 그랬어요.
sampleAnswer.en: I think there will be many people today. I should have made a reservation.

goal: Notice irregular verbs before they surprise you in real sentences.
scenario: You describe weather, walking, listening, and helping while forms change.
realLifeTask: Make three short sentences with irregular forms you actually need.
checkpoints: I can recognize ㅂ, ㄷ, 르, and ㅎ irregular patterns.
I can say 추워요, 걸어요, 들어요, and 빨라요 naturally.
I can check the stem before adding an ending.

sampleAnswer.ko: 오늘은 추워요. 그래서 빨리 걸었어요.
sampleAnswer.en: It is cold today. So I walked quickly.

goal: Use small particles to show who, for whom, only, also, and whose.
scenario: You talk about gifts, messages, belongings, and limits.
realLifeTask: Write one sentence with 에게/한테 and one with 도 or 만.
checkpoints: I can use 에게/한테 for a person receiving something.
I can use 도 for also and 만 for only.
I can use 의 carefully for possession or noun-to-noun links.

sampleAnswer.ko: 친구한테 메시지를 보냈어요. 저는 커피만 마셨어요.
sampleAnswer.en: I sent a message to my friend. I only drank coffee.

goal: Use counters in the places where Koreans expect them.
scenario: You buy drinks, count people, book tickets, or ask for quantity.
realLifeTask: Say three real quantities using counters like 잔, 명, 개, 번, or 장.
checkpoints: I can pair native numbers with common counters.
I can choose 잔, 명/분, 개, 장, 번, and 시간.
I can avoid translating English plurals directly.

sampleAnswer.ko: 커피 두 잔하고 티켓 세 장 주세요.
sampleAnswer.en: Please give me two cups of coffee and three tickets.

goal: Hear why Korean spelling and sound do not always match.
scenario: You listen to common words like 한국어, 같이, 국밥, and 학교.
realLifeTask: Pick three words from the chapter and read them aloud once from spelling, once from sound.
checkpoints: I can notice liaison when a final consonant moves before a vowel.
I can recognize common nasalization, aspiration, and tensification.
I can keep the original spelling even when the sound changes.

sampleAnswer.ko: 한국어는 한구거처럼 들리고, 같이라는 단어는 가치처럼 들려요.
sampleAnswer.en: 한국어 sounds like 한구거, and the word 같이 sounds like 가치.

goal: Choose the right kind of negative sentence for the situation.
scenario: You decline, say you cannot do something, or explain that something is not true.
realLifeTask: Make one 안 sentence, one 못 sentence, and one noun/adjective negative.
checkpoints: I can use 안 for not doing by choice or fact.
I can use 못 for cannot because of ability or situation.
I can use 아니에요 and -지 않아요 where short negation is not natural.

sampleAnswer.ko: 오늘은 못 가요. 시간이 없어서 공부도 많이 못 했어요.
sampleAnswer.en: I cannot go today. Because I do not have time, I also could not study much.

goal: Use 이다 forms when the sentence ends in a noun.
scenario: You explain identity, reason, contrast, or condition with noun sentences.
realLifeTask: Make one noun sentence, one reason clause, and one condition with 이다.
checkpoints: I can use 이에요/예요 after nouns.
I can use 이라서/라서 for because it is a noun.
I can use 이면/면 and 이고/고 with noun predicates.

sampleAnswer.ko: 오늘은 휴일이라서 사람이 많아요. 학생이면 할인이 돼요.
sampleAnswer.en: There are many people because today is a holiday. If you are a student, you get a discount.

goal: Talk about family and older relatives with the right respect.
scenario: You introduce family members or ask about someone else's family politely.
realLifeTask: Introduce one family member and say one respectful sentence about them.
checkpoints: I can choose family words like 어머니, 아버지, 부모님, and 동생.
I can use honorific forms when talking about older or respected family members.
I can avoid overusing casual family terms in polite situations.

sampleAnswer.ko: 저희 어머니는 부산에 사세요.
sampleAnswer.en: My mother lives in Busan.

goal: Explain symptoms and ask for help in a clinic or pharmacy.
scenario: You have a headache, stomachache, cold, or injury and need simple help.
realLifeTask: Say where it hurts, since when, and what you need.
checkpoints: I can use 아파요 with body parts.
I can use -부터 for when the symptom started.
I can make a polite request at a clinic or pharmacy.

sampleAnswer.ko: 어제부터 목이 아파요. 감기약이 필요해요.
sampleAnswer.en: My throat has hurt since yesterday. I need cold medicine.

goal: Talk about home problems and daily living needs.
scenario: Something in your room, apartment, or dorm is broken, missing, or hard to use.
realLifeTask: Describe one housing problem and ask someone to check or fix it.
checkpoints: I can name common home items and rooms.
I can use 고장 났어요, 안 돼요, and 필요해요.
I can ask politely for checking, repair, or help.

sampleAnswer.ko: 방에 불이 안 켜져요. 한번 확인해 주실 수 있어요?
sampleAnswer.en: The light in my room will not turn on. Could you check it once?

goal: Talk about weather in a way that connects to plans.
scenario: The weather changes what you wear, where you go, or whether you meet.
realLifeTask: Say today's weather and how it changes your plan.
checkpoints: I can describe weather with 덥다, 춥다, 흐리다, 비가 오다, and 눈이 오다.
I can connect weather to a result with -아서/어서 or -면.
I can use 것 같아요 for weather predictions.

sampleAnswer.ko: 오늘은 비가 올 것 같아요. 그래서 우산을 가져갈 거예요.
sampleAnswer.en: I think it will rain today. So I will bring an umbrella.

goal: Describe clothes and appearance without sounding too blunt.
scenario: You choose clothes, compliment a friend, or explain what someone is wearing.
realLifeTask: Describe one outfit and add one soft opinion or compliment.
checkpoints: I can use 입다, 신다, 쓰다, and 끼다 with the right item.
I can describe color, size, and fit before the noun.
I can soften appearance comments with 잘 어울려요 or 괜찮은 것 같아요.

sampleAnswer.ko: 오늘 입은 셔츠가 잘 어울려요. 색도 깔끔한 것 같아요.
sampleAnswer.en: The shirt you are wearing today suits you well. I think the color is clean too.

goal: Order and talk about Korean food beyond one-word menu names.
scenario: You choose a dish, ask about spice, and explain taste.
realLifeTask: Order one food and describe taste, spice, or preference.
checkpoints: I can ask if a food is spicy or contains an ingredient.
I can describe taste with 맵다, 짜다, 달다, 싱겁다, and 고소하다.
I can use 덜 or 빼 주세요 when ordering.

sampleAnswer.ko: 김치찌개 하나 주세요. 너무 매우면 고추를 조금만 넣어 주세요.
sampleAnswer.en: One kimchi stew, please. If it is too spicy, please add only a little chili.

goal: Talk about shows, music, games, and online life naturally.
scenario: You recommend content, explain what you watched, or talk about an app.
realLifeTask: Recommend one piece of content and say why someone might like it.
checkpoints: I can say 보다, 듣다, 올리다, 공유하다, and 추천하다 in digital contexts.
I can describe a show, song, or game with a noun modifier.
I can explain a recommendation with -아서/어서 or -거든요.

sampleAnswer.ko: 이 드라마 한번 봐 보세요. 대사가 쉬워서 한국어 공부에 좋아요.
sampleAnswer.en: Try watching this drama. The lines are easy, so it is good for studying Korean.

goal: Talk about school life, assignments, and study plans.
scenario: You ask about homework, deadlines, classes, and exams.
realLifeTask: Say what you need to study, by when, and what you will ask the teacher.
checkpoints: I can use 숙제, 시험, 수업, 발표, and 과제 in real sentences.
I can use -까지 for deadlines.
I can ask for explanation or feedback politely.

sampleAnswer.ko: 금요일까지 발표를 준비해야 해요. 선생님께 피드백을 부탁드릴 거예요.
sampleAnswer.en: I have to prepare the presentation by Friday. I will ask the teacher for feedback.

goal: Handle transport problems and route choices in more detail.
scenario: A bus is late, the subway is crowded, or you need to transfer.
realLifeTask: Explain one route, one problem, and one backup plan.
checkpoints: I can use 갈아타다, 내리다, 타다, 막히다, and 늦다.
I can use 로/으로 for route and transport.
I can explain delays with -아서/어서 or -는 바람에.

sampleAnswer.ko: 버스가 막혀서 늦을 것 같아요. 지하철로 갈아탈게요.
sampleAnswer.en: I think I will be late because the bus is stuck in traffic. I will transfer to the subway.

goal: Navigate Korean social habits without sounding rude or too casual.
scenario: You accept, decline, apologize, thank, or explain manners in a social setting.
realLifeTask: Write one polite acceptance, refusal, or apology for a real social situation.
checkpoints: I can use 죄송하지만 and 괜찮으시면 to soften a social sentence.
I can choose a polite expression for gifts, meals, or invitations.
I can explain a custom without overgeneralizing.

sampleAnswer.ko: 초대해 주셔서 감사해요. 그런데 오늘은 일이 있어서 못 갈 것 같아요.
sampleAnswer.en: Thank you for inviting me. But I think I cannot go today because I have work.

goal: Say who makes, lets, or has someone do something.
scenario: A parent feeds a child, a teacher has students read, or a manager seats guests.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: Did you look after your niece or nephew today?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes. I fed them and put them down for a nap too.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: When you went outside, did you put a coat on them too?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.en: Yes, I did. The toy made the child laugh.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 이렇게 보면 누가 누구에게 무엇을 하게 했는지가 보이네요.
dialogue.romanization: ireoke bomyeon nuga nuguege mueoseul hage haenneunjiga boineyo.
dialogue.en: Seen this way, you can tell who made someone do what.

realLifeTask: Describe one scene with a causative verb, then rewrite it with -게 하다.
checkpoints: I can find the person causing the action and the person doing it.
I can use common causatives like 먹이다, 입히다, 앉히다, 웃기다, and 울리다.
I can compare a built-in causative with V-게 하다.

sampleAnswer.ko: 선생님이 학생들에게 문장을 읽혔어요. 학생들이 문장을 읽게 했어요.
sampleAnswer.en: The teacher had the students read the sentence. The teacher made the students read the sentence.

goal: Use 겠 for formal intention, careful guessing, or polite softening.
scenario: You promise to handle something, infer a result, or politely decline.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.en: Could you check my order, please?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Yes, I will check it right away.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.en: There are many people, so it looks like it will take some time.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: Yes, it will take about ten minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Customer
dialogue.en: Then I will wait here.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: I will let you know as soon as it is ready.

realLifeTask: Make one sentence with -겠습니다 and one guess with -겠네요.
checkpoints: I can use -겠습니다 for a formal promise or service action.
I can use -겠네요 when I infer from evidence.
I can choose between 겠, -(으)ㄹ 거예요, and 것 같아요.

sampleAnswer.ko: 제가 확인하겠습니다. 자료를 보니 시간이 좀 걸리겠네요.
sampleAnswer.en: I will check it. Looking at the materials, it looks like it will take some time.

goal: Talk about a past choice that could have gone differently.
scenario: You missed a bus, found out too late, or wish you had said something earlier.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: I heard you were late for the interview yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네. 버스를 놓치지 않았더라면 늦지 않았을 텐데요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. beoseureul nochiji anatdeoramyeon neutji anasseul tende-yo.
dialogue.en: Yes. If I had not missed the bus, I would not have been late.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.en: If you had known in advance, would you have taken a taxi?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.ko: 네. 조금만 일찍 나왔으면 좋았을 텐데요.
dialogue.romanization: ne. jogeumman iljjik nawasseumyeon joasseul tende-yo.
dialogue.en: Yes. It would have been nice if I had left just a little earlier.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ko: 다음엔 전날에 길을 확인해 두면 좋겠어요.
dialogue.romanization: daeumen jeonnare gireul hwaginhae dumyeon jokesseoyo.
dialogue.en: Next time, it would be good to check the route the day before.

realLifeTask: Turn one real regret into an unreal conditional sentence.
checkpoints: I can use -았/었으면 for a soft regret or wish.
I can use -았/었더라면 for an unreal past condition.
I can pair the condition with -았/었을 텐데요 or -았/었을 거예요.

sampleAnswer.ko: 미리 알았더라면 더 일찍 출발했을 거예요.
sampleAnswer.en: If I had known in advance, I would have left earlier.

goal: Turn actions into nouns without making the sentence heavy.
scenario: You talk about studying, habits, goals, and things you saw someone do.
realLifeTask: Say one habit with -기 and one concrete action with -는 것.
checkpoints: I can use -기 for activities, goals, difficulty, and fixed forms.
I can use -는 것/거 for a specific action, fact, or event.
I can keep fixed expressions like -기로 했어요 and -기 전에.

sampleAnswer.ko: 매일 듣기가 어려워요. 그래도 문장을 따라 말하는 것이 도움이 돼요.
sampleAnswer.en: Listening every day is hard. Still, repeating sentences helps.

goal: Add the speaker's reaction at the end of the sentence.
scenario: You notice something, feel surprise, make a careful prediction, or express regret.
realLifeTask: React to one real situation with -네요, -군요, -ㄹ걸요, or -았/었을 텐데요.
checkpoints: I can use -네요 for a fresh realization.
I can use -군요 for a stronger or more formal realization.
I can use -ㄹ걸요 for a careful prediction and -았/었을 텐데요 for regret.

sampleAnswer.ko: 생각보다 어렵네요. 어제 조금 더 연습했으면 좋았을 텐데요.
sampleAnswer.en: It is harder than I expected. It would have been nice if I had practiced a little more yesterday.

goal: Choose 은/는 or 이/가 based on what the listener needs to notice.
scenario: You introduce new information, continue a topic, or contrast two people or things.
realLifeTask: Describe one real message or event using both 은/는 and 이/가.
checkpoints: I can use 이/가 for new or focused information.
I can use 은/는 for topic, contrast, or continuation.
I can build sentences like 이 문제는 이유가 중요해요.

sampleAnswer.ko: 친구가 연락했어요. 그 친구는 보통 메시지를 보내는데 오늘은 전화했어요.
sampleAnswer.en: A friend contacted me. That friend usually sends messages, but today they called.

goal: Make formal writing easier to follow with clear connectors.
scenario: You write a short report, complaint, summary, or project update.
realLifeTask: Write four formal sentences using two connectors such as 따라서, 그러나, 즉, or 결국.
checkpoints: I can choose a connector that matches the relationship between sentences.
I can keep formal connectors and formal endings in the same register.
I can revise a paragraph so the reader can follow the claim and reason.

sampleAnswer.ko: 자료가 부족합니다. 따라서 결론을 다시 검토해야 합니다. 그러나 핵심 주장은 유지할 수 있습니다.
sampleAnswer.en: The data is insufficient. Therefore, the conclusion must be reviewed again. However, the main claim can be maintained.

goal: Read casual Korean online without carrying it into formal writing.
scenario: You read comments, KakaoTalk messages, live chat, or social posts.
realLifeTask: Sort three expressions into friend chat, polite chat, and formal writing.
checkpoints: I can recognize ㅋㅋ, ㅠㅠ, ㅇㅇ, ㄹㅇ, and ㅇㅈ.
I can use casual intensifiers like 완전, 진짜, 대박, and 레전드 with the right people.
I can remove internet markers from formal email or school writing.

sampleAnswer.ko: 친구한테는 '완전 웃겨 ㅋㅋ'라고 해도 되지만, 공식 글에는 '재미있었습니다'라고 써야 해요.
sampleAnswer.en: To a friend, '완전 웃겨 ㅋㅋ' is okay, but in an official post, you should write 'it was interesting.'

goal: Put the whole course together in one message that fits the situation.
scenario: You switch between an interview answer, a formal email, coworker chat, and a KakaoTalk reply.
realLifeTask: Rewrite one idea for two different listeners, then check register, particles, tense, connectors, and closing.
checkpoints: I can choose the register before choosing vocabulary or endings.
I can check particles, tense, honorifics, connector, and closing in one pass.
I can rewrite the same meaning for formal email and casual chat.

sampleAnswer.ko: 메일에서는 '확인해 주셔서 감사합니다'라고 쓰고, 친구에게는 '확인해 줘서 고마워'라고 할게요.
sampleAnswer.en: In an email I will write 'thank you for checking,' and to a friend I will say 'thanks for checking.'
